Your healthcare professionals should give you clear information, talk with you about your or your child’s options, and listen carefully to your views and concerns. Your family can be involved too, if you wish. The study was comprised of three periods: Screening Period, Randomized Double-Blind Treatment Period, and an Open-Label Long Term Extension Period. ### Screening Period (3 to 4 weeks) This 3 to 4-week screening phase included study procedures to determine subject eligibility including, but not limited to: medical history, mutation analysis of ARG1 gene, arginase activity in RBCs, physical and neurological examination, EEG, ECG, and labs. Neuromotor function and neurocognitive assessments were also conducted during screening. Neuromotor assessments included the 2-Minute Walk Test (2MWT) and Gross Motor Function Measure-88 Parts D (GMFM-D) and E (GMFM-E). ### Randomized Double-Blind Treatment Period (24 weeks) Subjects were randomized 2:1 to receive: - Pegzilarginase IV infusion weekly + individualized disease management (IDM) for 24 weeks - Placebo IV infusion weekly + IDM for 24 weeks Subjects randomized to pegzilarginase began at Dose Level 2, 0.10 mg/kg. Beginning with Visit 5, dose modifications, if required based on arginine plasma concentrations (Cp), were implemented by the unblinded pharmacist and/or physician, according to an algorithm: - If arginine Cp was >150 µM, a single 168-hour sample was used to increase the dose by 2 dose levels (not to exceed 0.20 mg/kg) if the two doses prior to this sample were the same dose level in mg/kg and consecutive (no missed doses). - If arginine Cp from 2 sequential 168-hour samples (regardless of missed doses) are both <50 µM, the dose was decreased by 1 dose level, but not below 0.05 mg/kg. ### Long Term Extension (LTE) Period (up to ~150 weeks) **Blinded LTE Phase** The first 8 weeks of the LTE Period were blinded to ensure that study data relating to the randomized period were collected prior to unblinding. Subjects who were randomized to pegzilarginase received the optimized dose they received during the double-blind treatment period. Subjects who were randomized to placebo began the 8-week blinded treatment period at a dose of 0.10 mg/kg that could be adjusted during this period based on arginine Cp. **Open-Label LTE Phase** After the first 8 weeks of the Blinded LTE Phase, subjects had the option to receive open label pegzilarginase by subcutaneous (SC) injection (with investigator and sponsor approval). During this period, all subjects continued to receive IDM. The Phase 1/2 dosing was completed in February 2019, with 14 patients completing 8 weeks of repeat dosing. The trial investigated both single ascending doses and repeated dosing. The primary endpoint of the trial was safety and tolerability of intravenous administration of pegzilarginase in patients with Arginase 1 Deficiency. METHODS: We report the first Italian real-world experience with pegzilarginase in three pediatric patients with genetically confirmed ARG1-D enrolled in the phase 3 PEACE trial. ## Languages * eng ## Abstract BACKGROUND: Arginase 1 deficiency (ARG1-D) is an ultra-rare urea cycle disorder characterized by hyperargininemia and progressive neurological impairment, including spasticity, loss of motor function, and reduced quality of life. Conventional management based on dietary protein restriction and ammonia scavengers rarely achieves adequate metabolic control or prevents neurological deterioration. Pegzilarginase, a recombinant human arginase 1 enzyme, is the first disease-modifying therapy for ARG1-D. METHODS: We report the first Italian real-world experience with pegzilarginase in three pediatric patients with genetically confirmed ARG1-D enrolled in the phase 3 PEACE trial. Clinical, biochemical, functional, nutritional and quality-of-life data were retrospectively collected over a long-term follow-up (2003-2025).
